content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To cook beef tongue, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Rinse the raw tongue under cold running water (5 minutes)
Step 2. Peel away the thick outer skin after the first boil (15 minutes)
Step 3. Discard the initial blanching liquid (2 minutes)
Step 4. Prepare a fresh pot of filtered water (3 minutes)
Step 5. Add peppercorns and bay leaves to the pot (1 minute)
Step 6. Skim the foam from the surface of the simmering liquid (10 minutes)
Step 7. Place the tongue in a large stockpot (2 minutes)
Step 8. Dice carrots and celery for the aromatic base (10 minutes)
Step 9. Reduce heat to a very low simmer (1 minute)
Step 10. Slice a large yellow onion into quarters (3 minutes)
Step 11. Bring the pot to a rolling boil (20 minutes)
Step 12. Measure out whole cloves and allspice berries (2 minutes)
Step 13. Scrub the tongue with a stiff kitchen brush (5 minutes)
Step 14. Add a pinch of sea salt (30 seconds)
Step 15. Toast the spices in a dry pan to release oils (4 minutes)
Step 16. Gather all necessary herbs and spices from the pantry (5 minutes)
Step 17. Submerge the tongue fully in the cooking liquid (1 minute)
Step 18. Check the water level to ensure it covers the meat (1 minute)
Step 19. Trim excess fat and gristle from the root of the tongue (8 minutes)
Step 20. Add the quartered onions to the pot (1 minute)
Step 21. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid (30 seconds)
Step 22. Prepare a bowl of ice water for shocking the meat (5 minutes)
Step 23. Pat the meat dry with paper towels (3 minutes)
Step 24. Sharpen your carving knife (10 minutes)
Step 25. Peel several cloves of garlic (4 minutes)
Step 26. Simmer the meat until fork-tender (3 hours)
Step 27. Test the internal temperature with a probe (1 minute)
Step 28. Sauté the aromatic vegetables in butter (12 minutes)
Step 29. Strain the cooking broth through a fine-mesh sieve (10 minutes)
Step 30. Locate the large stockpot in the bottom cabinet (2 minutes)
Step 31. Chill the cooked tongue in the fridge to firm it up (4 hours)
Step 32. Prepare a workspace on a large cutting board (5 minutes)
Step 33. Adjust the seasoning of the broth (2 minutes)
Step 34. Label a storage container for leftovers (2 minutes)
Step 35. Clear space in the refrigerator (5 minutes)
Step 36. Blanch the tongue for the first time (15 minutes)
Step 37. Remove the tongue from the boiling water (2 minutes)
Step 38. Slice the meat into thin, even rounds (15 minutes)
Step 39. Reserve a cup of the concentrated cooking liquid (2 minutes)
Step 40. Purchase a high-quality beef tongue from the butcher (1 hour)
Step 41. Let the meat rest on a carving board (20 minutes)
Step 42. Transfer the tongue to a clean plate (2 minutes)
Step 43. Deglaze the vegetable pan with a splash of wine (5 minutes)
Step 44. Clean the sink and preparation area (15 minutes)
Step 45. Arrange the slices on a serving platter (5 minutes)
Step 46. Wash the fresh parsley and thyme (5 minutes)
Step 47. Check the expiration date on the spices (2 minutes)
Step 48. Combine the sautéed vegetables with the broth (5 minutes)
Step 49. Ladle some hot broth over the meat (2 minutes)
Step 50. Prepare a side of horseradish sauce (10 minutes)
Step 51. Set the stovetop timer (1 minute)
Step 52. Allow the meat to cool slightly for easier handling (30 minutes)
Step 53. Garnish the dish with fresh herbs (3 minutes)
Step 54. Verify the tenderness with a small paring knife (1 minute)
Step 55. Reduce the strained broth to make a glaze (25 minutes)
Step 56. Reheat the sliced meat gently in the glaze (8 minutes)
Step 57. Mince the garlic cloves (5 minutes)
Step 58. Chop the fresh herbs finely (6 minutes)
Step 59. Wipe down the stove surface (10 minutes)
Step 60. Whisk a bit of flour into the vegetables for thickness (4 minutes)
Step 61. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife (2 minutes)
Step 62. Sprinkle with cracked black pepper (30 seconds)
Step 63. Prepare the bouquet garni with kitchen twine (10 minutes)
Step 64. Drain the blanching water into the sink (2 minutes)
Step 65. Serve the beef tongue while warm (2 minutes)
Step 66. Cool the broth to room temperature (1 hour)
Step 67. Remove the tongue from the pot after the long simmer (3 minutes)
Step 68. Taste the final sauce for balance (1 minute)
Step 69. Plate the vegetables alongside the meat (4 minutes)
Step 70. Turn off the burner (30 seconds)
Step 71. Discard the tough outer skin (2 minutes)
Step 72. Place the tongue back into the seasoned broth (5 minutes)
Step 73. Steel the knife edge for a final hone (2 minutes)
Step 74. Prepare the aromatics for the second stage (10 minutes)
Step 75. Pour the finished sauce over the platter (2 minutes)
Step 76. Thaw the meat if it was previously frozen (12 hours)
Step 77. Finely chop the parsley for garnish (5 minutes)
Step 78. Select a fresh beef tongue from the refrigerator (1 minute)
Step 79. Reduce the heat for the final glaze thickening (5 minutes)
Step 80. Present the completed dish to the table (1 minute)
